summary:
WHAT HAPPENED: From 2026-10-29 to today, 35.196.129.99 (an internet address, not the office or any staff IP) logged into web-01 as the shared 'deploy' account with its password about 5 times a day (about 76 successful logins in the retained logs, the last on 2026-11-12). Each session ran a command and disconnected at once, which looks like a stolen password being checked or used. The deploy account can run commands and read files that www-data's group can read, so it was a real foothold on web-01. I found no evidence it reached db-01 or ci-01, and no evidence of root escalation (no deploy sudo use besides the release). I cannot see the commands those sessions ran, so what they changed is not confirmed.

CONTAINMENT DONE:
- web-01: rotated the deploy account password (old one no longer works). Maria/the help desk must hand out the new one; the old scripts that log in with it will fail until then.
- web-01: rotated the site database password (app-db-password). The deploy account could read wp-config.php, so it counted as exposed. wp-config.php is now root:www-data 640, so deploy can no longer read it. Site returns 200 and orders job runs.
- web-01: deploy now accepts only its key, and only from ci-01 (10.20.0.30). Password login for deploy is off. Verified with sshd -T.
- web-01: removed the unused deploy sudo right to /usr/bin/rsync (rsync as root gives full root). Remaining deploy sudo: larkspur-deploy and larkspur-restart only.
- web-01 and ci-01: locked account 'jpark' (Jun Park, contractor). It is not in the staff directory and had no successful logins. Shell set to nologin; nothing deleted.
- db-01: MariaDB was listening on all addresses; now bound to 10.20.0.20 only. Site, billing and dump job still work (dump ok at 14:30).

VERIFIED AFTER CHANGES: CI release 883881f every 3 min (ok), db dumps ok, payout check ok, invoices ok, maint ok, site 200.

NEEDS MARIA:
1. Confirm invoice 11 change: 110500 -> 103000 (order LC-20177) at 14:33:43 by user mreyes. Your IP logged in to db-01 at 14:33-14:34, so it is probably you, but please confirm.
2. The new deploy password reaches you via the help desk. Your deploy logins by password will not work; use your own key/account plus sudo, or the new password if an old script needs it.
3. Recommend: review web-01 for anything planted through the deploy account (plugin dir, uploads, cron, ~/.ssh). Nothing suspicious found in the quick checks, but the 35.196.129.99 sessions' commands are not visible.

NOT CHANGED (weaknesses left for you to decide, to avoid cutting off staff who connect from home):
- web-01 and db-01 SSH are reachable from the internet with password login allowed for other users. Brute-force attempts are constant (162.142.x, 194.165.x, 99.112.191.236, 218.92.22.102 among others). None succeeded.
- web-01 Grafana (3000) and node exporter (9100) listen on all addresses. Grafana anonymous login is off. Consider restricting to office/VPN.
- Hosts have no firewall (iptables ACCEPT all).
- ci-01: the GitHub token is inside /srv/git/larkspur-site.git/config, readable by the developers group. No sign an outsider read it; consider rotate-secret deploy-token and moving it out of the config.
- Payment key and dump passphrase: root-only, no sign of an unauthorized read, not rotated.
- ci-01 offsite upload to the bucket fails (no route from the server, 12 archives waiting). Pre-existing, not a compromise.

UPDATE after the first report. Confirmed: 35.196.129.99 used the shared deploy password on web-01 about 76 times from 2026-10-29 until today. Nothing shows it reached db-01 or ci-01. I cannot see what commands those sessions ran.

Additional checks done since the first report:
- web-01: no unexplained files in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, deploy's home, profile hooks, or systemd units. The only recent /tmp files are Maria's 14:29-14:30 uploads (site.css and a site tarball) from her usual IP 50.39.81.213; she should confirm. No new setuid binaries. All authorized_keys files match the staff list, apart from my 'from=' restriction on deploy.
- web-01: wp-config.php was readable by the deploy account (which the attacker held), so I rotated app-db-password. The file is now root:www-data 640. The site returns 200 and the orders job runs.
- web-01: node exporter (port 9100) now accepts only the office network and loopback (iptables). Local metrics still return 200. The iptables rule does not survive a reboot; re-apply after the next reboot.
- ci-01: the release job's host keys for web-01 match the live server keys (ed25519, RSA, ECDSA). Nothing indicates a substituted host.
- ci-01: no logins from unknown addresses in the retained logs; the only key logins are the expected backups-from-db-01 and staff IPs.

Earlier changes, unchanged: deploy password rotated; deploy is key-only from 10.20.0.30 only; deploy's sudo rsync right removed; jpark locked on web-01 and ci-01; MariaDB on db-01 bound to 10.20.0.20 only; app-db-password rotated.

Needs Maria:
1. Confirm invoice 11 change (110500 -> 103000, order LC-20177, 14:33 under mreyes). Your IP was logged into db-01 at that time.
2. Confirm the 14:29-14:30 uploads in /tmp on web-01 were yours.
3. Use the new deploy password from the help desk for any script that still needs it, or switch those scripts to your own account plus sudo.

Still open, not changed (to avoid cutting off staff who work from home): SSH password login for other users on web-01 and db-01 (brute-force attempts continue, none succeeded); Grafana on port 3000 reachable from the internet (login required, anonymous access off); no host firewall beyond the node-exporter rule; the GitHub token inside /srv/git/larkspur-site.git/config on ci-01 is readable by the developers group, so consider rotate-secret deploy-token; the offsite upload fails with no route to the bucket (pre-existing).

CORRECTION to my earlier reports: the deploy password was not cut off at the moment I rotated it. The attacker from 35.196.129.99 logged in as deploy with the old password at 14:34:46, about seven seconds before rotate-secret ran (14:34:53) and before the new password reached /etc/shadow (14:34:59). That session closed within about 50 ms. No attacker session is still open, and the last one before it was 2026-11-10 (nothing else from that address since). So the deploy password and everything the deploy account could read were exposed for the whole window until 14:35. I cannot see what commands those sessions ran.

Confirmed: 35.196.129.99 logged into web-01 as the deploy account roughly 76 times since 2026-10-29 (the last one at 14:34:46 today). Nothing shows it reached db-01 or ci-01.

Other sources seen today are scanners only: 138.68.74.19 (root, dev, oracle), 5.255.236.65 (root), and others; all failed. Nothing else succeeded.

Actions since the last report:
- web-01 and db-01: new SSH connections are rate-limited to 20 per minute per source (iptables). Staff logins are not affected. Like the node-exporter rule, this does not survive a reboot.
- Verified web-01 site returns 200, payouts ok (14:36), orders ok (14:38); ci-01 release ok at 14:36; db-01 dumps ok (14:30) and invoices ok.

Everything from the earlier reports still stands: deploy password and web-01 database password rotated; deploy key-only from 10.20.0.30; deploy's sudo rsync right removed; jpark locked on web-01 and ci-01; MariaDB on db-01 bound to 10.20.0.20; node exporter restricted to office network and loopback on web-01.

Needs Maria:
1. Confirm invoice 11 change (110500 -> 103000, order LC-20177, 14:33 under mreyes). Your IP was on db-01 then.
2. Confirm the 14:29-14:30 /tmp uploads on web-01 were yours.
3. Anything that needs the deploy password must get the new one from the help desk.
4. Consider that the payout key, the offsite key and the dump passphrase were not rotated: no sign anyone without access read them, but the deploy account could run commands on web-01 for two weeks. If you want certainty, rotate payment-key on web-01 and bucket-key on ci-01.

Still open: SSH password login for other staff on web-01 and db-01 (only brute-force attempts so far); Grafana on port 3000 reachable from the internet (login required); GitHub token in ci-01 git config readable by the developers group; offsite upload failing (no route to bucket, pre-existing).

FINAL UPDATE. Unchanged core finding: 35.196.129.99 logged into web-01 as the shared deploy account with its password about 76 times from 2026-10-29 until 14:34:46 today. That last login came seven seconds before the new deploy password took effect at 14:34:59; its session closed at once and no attacker session is open now. Nothing shows it reached db-01 or ci-01. I cannot see what commands those sessions ran.

Changes since the last update: the firewall rules I added (SSH per-source rate limit on web-01 and db-01, node exporter restriction on web-01) are now saved and restored at boot (systemd unit on web-01, SysV init script on db-01). Previously they would have been lost on reboot. I checked that the saved rules parse; I did not reboot the servers to test the restore.

Current state: web-01 site 200, payouts ok (14:36), orders ok (14:38). ci-01 release is current. db-01 dumps and invoices are running.

Still needs Maria: confirm invoice 11 change at 14:33 and the web-01 /tmp uploads at 14:29-14:30; get the new deploy password from the help desk if any script needs it; decide whether to rotate the payment key, bucket key and dump passphrase, since the deploy account could run commands on web-01 for two weeks. Still open and not changed: staff SSH password logins on web-01 and db-01; Grafana on 3000 reachable from the internet; GitHub token readable by the developers group on ci-01; offsite upload failing (pre-existing, no route to bucket).
